title: Texas's 35th Congressional District election, 2026
jurisdiction: Texas's 35th Congressional District — Bexar, Guadalupe, Wilson, and Karnes counties
description: The 2026 election for Texas's 35th Congressional District is an open-seat race following 2025 redistricting that drew incumbent Democrat Greg Casar out of the district and reconfigured the boundaries to favor Republicans. The newly drawn district covers parts of San Antonio and outlying areas in Bexar, Guadalupe, Wilson, and Karnes counties; Trump would have carried it by about 10 points in 2024, and the Cook Political Report rates it R+4. Democrat Johnny Garcia, a Bexar County Sheriff's Deputy and self-described 'old-school law-and-order Democrat,' faces Republican Carlos De La Cruz, a retired 20-year Air Force veteran and brother of U.S. Rep. Monica De La Cruz, in what is expected to be one of the most competitive House races in Texas. Both candidates won their party's primary runoffs on May 26, 2026, setting up a general election contest that will test whether Democrats can hold a Hispanic-majority district redrawn at the request of President Trump.
polling_note: No public opinion polls for the TX-35 general election were found as of the research date. The Cook Political Report rates the race as Lean Republican (R+4).

candidates.name: Johnny Garcia
candidates.summary: Johnny Garcia is a Bexar County Sheriff's Deputy and the Democratic nominee for Texas's 35th Congressional District. A lifelong San Antonio resident, he worked construction jobs while attending community college before joining the Bexar County Sheriff's Office, where he served in the jail, patrol, SWAT Crisis Negotiation Team, and as Public Information Officer for the past seven years. Garcia pitches himself as an 'old-school, law-and-order Democrat' focused on reducing tariffs, increasing federal grants for local law enforcement, preventing congressional stock trading, and strengthening public education.

candidates.name: Carlos De La Cruz
candidates.summary: Carlos De La Cruz is a retired 20-year U.S. Air Force veteran and the Republican nominee for Texas's 35th Congressional District. He enlisted at age 18, served multiple post-9/11 deployments to the Middle East and assignments along the southern border conducting counter-narcotics operations, and later co-owned a kickboxing gym in San Antonio with his wife. De La Cruz, who is the brother of U.S. Rep. Monica De La Cruz (R-TX-15), has been endorsed by President Donald Trump and emphasizes border security, American energy independence, cutting government spending, and supporting law enforcement.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polling exists for TX-35. This forecast relies on district-fundamental signals provided in the race data. The 2025 redistricting drew incumbent Democrat Greg Casar out and reconfigured the boundaries to favor Republicans; Trump would have carried the new district by roughly 10 points in 2024, and Cook Political Report rates it R+4. Both factors point to a Republican edge. However, the district is Hispanic-majority and covers parts of San Antonio, giving Democrats a plausible coalitional path, and both nominees are credible candidates. The lack of any polling keeps uncertainty elevated, preventing a higher-confidence rating. The race is rated Lean Republican with a modest margin estimate consistent with the Cook R+4 baseline.
